key_insight: For periodic DFT, the best learned initializer is not necessarily the most accurate offline predictor; it must actually speed up the SCF solver trajectory.
engineering_relevance: This study shows how to evaluate ML electronic-state predictors in the loop, revealing whether they reduce SCF iterations and runtime rather than just prediction error.
method: Built ρHD-43K, a 43,851-crystal corpus with aligned density, Hamiltonian, and density-matrix labels.
Extended the SCF workflow to inject predicted density, Hamiltonian, or density-matrix states.
Compared direct converged-state prediction and residual prediction against solver-native references on frozen non-magnetic test crystals.
evidence_signal: On the test set, oracle density-matrix or Hamiltonian injection reduced the median SCF count from 16 to 1, while direct charge-density prediction (Charge3Net-E3) sped up about 91% of paired crystals and achieved a 1.18× SCF-loop speedup.
watch_item: Offline accuracy alone is not a reliable proxy for solver utility; some residual initializers did not consistently outperform the superposition-of-atomic-densities baseline.
paper_title: Evaluating Predicted Densities, Hamiltonians, and Density Matrices as Periodic SCF Initializers
